guideline: annotators scored each CS across these four dimensions: Cogency (COG), Suitableness (SUI), Relevance (REL), and Informativeness (INF) on a 1-5 Likert scale
Annotators were given annotation guidelines and examples, then rated each counterspeech on the four dimensions using a Likert scale.

We rely on the following four dimensions defined on a 1-5 Likert scale: Cogency (COG) measures the amount and logical correctness of the supporting arguments provided by the CS: we use an adapted version of this metric from . Suitableness (SUI) measures how much a CS has a suitable style, meaning that it is polite, not hateful, it attacks the message and not the hater . Moreover, the CS should defend the minority attacked by the HS. Relevance (REL) measures how relevant the CS is to the content of the corresponding HS in terms of topic and target of hate . Informativeness (INF) measures how informative the CS is as a response to its HS in terms of the quantity and factual correctness of included facts .
